Bangkok Dusit Medical Services (BDMS) has achieved the top global ranking in the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices (DJSI) 2024, securing the highest score in the Health Care Services and Providers Industry category on both DJSI World and DJSI Emerging Markets, as recognized by the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) 2024.
BDMS received an 'AA' rating in the MSCI ESG Ratings for 2024.
BDMS was selected as a member of the FTSE4Good Index Series for the 9th consecutive year.
BDMS was awarded a prestigious 5-star rating in corporate governance by the Thai Institute of Directors.
BDMS won 2 awards in the Business Excellence category at the SET Awards 2024 - Best Investor Relations Awards and Best Innovative Company Awards.
BDMS received 3 awards from the Investment Analysts Association (IAA), including Best CEO, Best CFO, and Best Investor Relations.
BDMS was awarded Outstanding Role Model Organization in 'Human Rights Award 2024' in large business category from the Rights and Liberties Protection Department, Ministry of Justice.
BDMS is committed to enhancing healthcare quality in line with international standards.
All hospitals are accredited to international standards to ensure safe and efficient treatment.
12 hospitals have been designated as Centers of Excellence, providing specialized care in various medical fields.

BDMS implements the Hub-and-Spoke model, in which highly specialized hospitals (Hubs) provide advanced care for critically ill patients, while smaller hospitals (Spokes) manage patients with mild to moderate conditions.
BDMS has developed a telemedicine system to expand access to healthcare services, enabling patients to receive remote consultations and continuous care.

BDMS strengthens its healthcare services through various healthcare-related businesses, including medical laboratories, pharmaceuticals, saline production, pharmacies, and medical equipment distribution.

Through continuous innovation, strategic healthcare expansion, and adherence to international medical standards, BDMS remains a leader in healthcare excellence, reinforcing Thailand’s position as a regional hub for world-class medical services.
BDMS strengthens its global partnerships to provide modern, high-quality healthcare services, ensuring that patients receive cutting-edge treatment and comprehensive care.
BDMS is dedicated to becoming a value-based healthcare provider, emphasizing sustainable healthcare solutions that prioritize patient health, treatment effectiveness, and cost efficiency.

BDMS continuously works to advance medical outcomes, enhance the quality of care, increase access to comprehensive healthcare services, and reduce overall healthcare costs, contributing to a more sustainable healthcare system.

BDMS upholds the highest standards of good governance, quality, and safety while ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, respecting human rights, and taking full responsibility for social and environmental impacts across the value chain.
BDMS has consistently received industry recognition and numerous awards, affirming its leadership in medical excellence, sustainability, and healthcare innovation.

BDMS conducts an annual sustainability materiality assessment covering internal and external factors that positively and negatively impact on the economy, society, the environment, and human rights, as outlined in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) framework.

BDMS’s sustainability materiality topics are identified based on “Double Materiality” considering both impact materiality (BDMS’s influence on the economy, environment, and society) and financial materiality (environmental and social impact on corporate financial performance and business values).

BDMS integrates sustainability materiality into the risk management process in service quality and patient safety, cybersecurity and data protection, occupational health and safety, human capital development and retention as well as energy management and climate change.
claims.section: Integrating Sustainability Materiality into Risk Management

claims.claim_text: BDMS utilizes financial risk criteria to assess the financial impact of each materiality topic and adopts the Double Materiality approach to effectively identify and manage critical risks, drive appropriate risk management strategies and allocate resources for mitigation measures to address potential impacts comprehensively.
claims.section: Integrating Sustainability Materiality into Risk Management

claims.claim_text: In 2024, BDMS reaffirmed its commitment to sustainability by maintaining the materiality topics identified in 2023, reflecting a consistent and strategic approach to long-term environmental, social, and governance (ESG) priorities.
To ensure credibility and transparency, the review process and assessment outcomes from 2023 were independently verified by an external organization unaffiliated with BDMS’s business and operations.
BDMS has conducted a stakeholder assessment and analysis in accordance with the AA1000 Stakeholder Engagement Standard (AA1000SES).
Supply Chain Management aligns with GRI standards 308-1, 414-1 and addresses SDGs 4.4, 5.1, 8.3, 8.7, 9.4, 12.7.
Customer Relationship Management aligns with GRI 418 and addresses SDGs 16.7.
Community Engagement aligns with GRI 201-1 and addresses SDGs 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6.
Occupational Health and Safety aligns with safeguarding employees, doctors, and dentists.
Respecting Human Rights aligns with GRI standards 405-1, 412 and addresses SDGs 5.1, 5.2, 8.5, 8.8, 10.3, 16.3.
Circular Economy aligns with GRI standards 306-3, 306-4, 306-5 and addresses SDGs 12.3, 12.4, 12.5.
Water Stewardship aligns with GRI standards 303-3, 303-4, 303-5 and addresses SDGs 6.3, 6.4, 12.2.

BDMS is committed to developing an efficient internal management mechanism that creates proper and sustainable benefits while considering the rights and expectations of all stakeholders across all sectors.
BDMS has established a clear corporate governance framework as a guideline for the collaboration among the Board of Directors, executives, and employees of all levels within the organization.

With a strong commitment to conducting a transparent, fair, verifiable and ethical business, BDMS has been awarded a five-star rating in Corporate Governance in 2024 from the Corporate Governance Report of Thai Listed Companies (CGR) by the Thai Institute of Directors (IOD).
BDMS is dedicated to conducting a transparent, fair, ethical and verifiable business in alignment with anti-corruption principles as stated in the BDMS Code of Ethics.
In 2024, BDMS reviewed and updated the Anti-corruption Policy to ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and international standards.
BDMS remains committed to integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles into its core business strategy.
BDMS has established a comprehensive risk management framework focusing on three key aspects to ensure business resilience and sustainability.
BDMS is committed to proactive risk management by identifying potential safety risks and implementing preventive measures to mitigate patient risks.
BDMS ensures continuous risk monitoring and evaluation, enabling a swift and effective response to emerging challenges while maintaining business resilience and operational excellence.

BDMS has integrated data on significant risk issues, including global risk factors and risks at the medical industry level, along with the organization’s key material issues to ensure that the framework for risk issues encompasses all dimensions related to the organization’s operations.
BDMS places patient safety as a top priority and is committed to ensuring that all subsidiaries continuously improve and enhance healthcare quality.

BDMS, in collaboration with Thai Airways International Public Company Limited, organized the “Safety Culture Workshop” to integrate aviation safety management principles into the healthcare service system.
Following the workshop, BDMS developed animated learning materials on Non-Technical Skills: Situational Awareness, making it a mandatory training module in November 2024.
The training engaged 24,046 participants, achieving an average score of 4.5 out of 5.
In 2024 Patient Safety Culture Survey Score Increased by 74%
BDMS mandates safety culture training for both new and existing doctors and dentists across its subsidiaries.
In 2024, all 800 new doctors and dentists who participated in the training achieved a 100% completion or success rate.
The contingency drill for computer malfunction demonstrated a 97% completion rate in executing the required procedures.

Feedback and suggestions from the drill will be communicated to relevant departments to enhance future operational efficiency and preparedness, ensuring continuous improvement in system resilience and response strategies.
The organization achieved full (100%) crisis management plan testing in 2024, surpassing the stated minimum target of 90%.
The metric indicates that the After Action Review follow-up rate has met the target exactly, achieving 100% completion against a 100% goal.

BDMS ensures the system is agile and flexible while assessing and mitigating cybersecurity risks to provide an efficient digital transformation that enhances business capabilities while coping with the rapidly shifting technology and artificial intelligence trends.

BDMS sets the governance structure for information security as well as enforces policies, guidelines, and operational standards for the subsidiaries to ensure the appropriate use of information technology and systems as well as prevent potential risks.

The BDMS IT Governance Committee, led by Mr. Chairat Panthuraamphorn, M.D., has been established to devise information technology strategies and ensure their implementation within hospital networks and other businesses supporting the hospitals.

The Committee supports the management of security protection, privacy, digital assets and data integrity in line with the Information Security Management Policy, other globally recognized standards as well as domestic and international regulations.

The Committee also manages information systems, safeguards data security, and creates communication networks to ensure data protection following global standards and legal requirements in Thailand and abroad.
BDMS develops user-friendly and accessible channels for submitting requests and complaints to ensure rapid and effective flow.
BDMS regularly assesses and evaluates the process to ensure compliance with data protection regulations and standards.

BDMS has signed data sharing agreements within its network to maximize customer benefits while ensuring that all operations related to personal data are conducted securely and in line with the regulations.
The agreements signed among BDMS subsidiaries standardize procedures for managing and sharing data while enhancing collaboration and operation efficiency between entities.
Other objectives are to protect the data privacy of stakeholders and mitigate risks associated with data breaches.

BDMS is committed to maximizing the value of medical services and healthcare to ensure exceptional patient experience while operating with expertise, dedication, and adherence to medical ethics and transparency.
claims.section: Marketing Communication, Sales and Labeling Guidelines

claims.claim_text: BDMS implements the marketing communication, sales and medication labeling guidelines in accordance with international standards, ensuring transparency and providing patients with accurate information about medications and treatments following their needs.
claims.section: Marketing Communication, Sales and Labeling Guidelines

claims.claim_text: BDMS recognizes the importance of innovation and fostering a culture of innovation to enhance service efficiency.

This is achieved through the application of digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI), with the goal of achieving a smart hospital that can deliver the highest service experiences, ultimately leading to ongoing improvements in business performance.

BDMS devises supply chain planning and assesses corporate risks while implementing comprehensive risk management strategies for supply chain management with an objective to ensure efficient services to customers, elevate the well-being of the Thais, and maintain national public health security.

The BDMS supply chain management is overseen by the BDMS Central Procurement Department, operating in accordance with strategies and policies reviewed by the BDMS Supply Chain and Resource Management Committee, is in charge of BDMS supply chain management.

BDMS introduces key strategies as the core factors for supply chain management by integrating sustainability materiality topics into the corporate supply chain criteria in line with the corporate mission and vision.

Establish a centralized procurement system to consolidate procurement in all BDMS networks while enhancing value chain efficiency and utmost transparency in line with international regulations and standards as well as corporate strategies.
Integrate sustainable procurement to achieve fair, honest, transparent and ethical business operations while adopting sustainability materiality into supplier selection and procurement criteria.
Develop strategic supplier partnerships to foster on building collaborations with key suppliers to drive sustainable growth.

BDMS mandates the Human Resource Department to oversee the management of Human Capital Management by cultivating an organizational culture that sets the direction and jointly defined goals for employee practices, aligning them with the organization’s strategic plans and objectives.
BDMS aims to clarify career advancement pathways and drive towards organizational goals while taking care of the well-being of valued employee.
BDMS has developed a human resource management strategy adhering to 3 key principles.

Developing employee with essential additional skills, including learning innovative technology, to promote the advancement of employees in their career paths and ensure readiness to perform efficiently.
BDMS focuses on delivering excellent healthcare services by enhancing knowledge and skills from the first day of employment.
BDMS has developed a training and development strategy that is crucial for the sustainable development of the organization, covering both clinical and non-clinical roles within the hospital.

Bangkok Hospital Headquarter has implemented the BHQ Employee Wellness program, establishing the Employee Wellness Committee (EWC) to analyze mental and physical health issues arising from work and the work environment.
The objective is to develop employee wellness promotion plans and enhance benefits for employees at Bangkok Hospital Headquarters, targeting 100% participation in the annual health check-up program.

A Staff Clinic has been established for employee medical examinations and treatment, taking into account work-life balance, appropriate work schedule management, and organizing activities that promote the health of employees and their families.
Bangkok Hospital Phitsanulok has implemented the “WeFit for All” program to develop a Digital Platform innovation for employee health care.
The program aims to track and evaluate health outcomes according to established goals, such as weight loss, weight gain, muscle strength improvement, and sports fitness levels.
There is a clear upward trend in customer retention at BDMS from 2020 to 2024, rising from 85.00% to 93.77%.

claims.claim_text: BDMS emphasizes the importance of respecting fundamental rights. Therefore, it has integrated healthcare workforce resources, modern healthcare innovations and technologies, and the readiness provided by its network of hospitals and supporting medical businesses.

This integration aims to enhance and expand access to healthcare services, contributing to supportive initiatives for Thai society and ensuring that disadvantaged individuals receive equitable access to comprehensive healthcare services.
Launch a total of 4,500 initiatives related to healthcare access for the communities across Thailand, compared to the baseline year 2022.
BDMS acknowledges the critical public health issues and opportunities related to promoting access to healthcare services and well-being for disadvantaged and vulnerable groups in Thailand.
BDMS has initiated various community-based programs through collaboration with interdisciplinary healthcare professionals, leveraging organizational capacity and expertise to drive these initiatives.

BDMS also partners with non-profit charitable organizations, such as the Vejdusit Foundation under the Royal Patronage of H.R.H. Princess Galyani Vadhana Krom Luang Naradhiwas Rajanagarindra to implement social programs aimed at enhancing health equity and improving quality of life sustainably.

Proactive Health Management: Conducting comprehensive health assessments to identify early-stage health concerns, thereby enabling preventive measures and timely interventions for both short-term and long-term health outcomes.
Enhancing Access to Healthcare: Expanding access to essential medical services in accordance with fundamental rights, ensuring that individuals can maintain stable and sustainable living conditions.
Empowerment through Education: Providing knowledge and essential skills for health promotion and hygiene, contributing to the overall improvement of quality of life.
BDMS has implemented comprehensive safety guidelines and well-being initiatives to enhance occupational health and safety, boost employee morale, and foster a positive workplace culture.
Through proactive measures, the organization minimizes workplace risks, ensuring a safe and secure environment for all employees.
Integrating safety protocols across all operational levels guarantees that employees are well-protected, informed, and equipped to maintain high work efficiency and job satisfaction.
BDMS emphasizes the broader impacts of its operations, encouraging employees to consider environmental and social implications throughout the supply chain.

BDMS has implemented a comprehensive occupational health and safety system in alignment with Hospital Accreditation (HA), Joint Commission International (JCI), and other relevant occupational health regulations.
BDMS ensures that its services prioritize the physical and mental well-being of employees, alongside their workplace safety.
BDMS has implemented a structured approach through key policies and committees.
The Occupational Health, Safety, and Environment Policy, which is reviewed annually, ensures adherence to regulatory compliance and best practices.

BDMS has established the Occupational Health, Safety, and Environment Committee across all business units, responsible for conducting risk assessments, implementing workplace safety measures for both healthcare and non-healthcare activities, and ensuring operational continuity while maintaining safety and environmental standards.

In 2024, BDMS will continue to promote the holistic health of employees through health programs and the creation of a conducive working environment to reduce injuries and illnesses arising from work and workloads, with a goal of reducing work-related fatalities to zero.

The company has communicated occupational health and workplace environmental policies and practices to employees through various channels, such as organizational emails, YouTube, and the BDMS People Connect application, to provide comprehensive and up-to-date information.

BDMS also prioritizes the selection of partners and contractors who comply with occupational health and safety standards, using strict criteria and requirements for procurement, such as adherence to safety regulations, safety training.

In 2024, the hospital will provide fire emergency response training for all employees to ensure compliance with safety standards effectively and reduce the risk of fire emergencies in healthcare facilities.
Additionally, there will be an ongoing development of risk assessment plans to improve the infrastructure and essential utilities necessary for maintaining safety in existing buildings.
For 2024, the hospital will conduct comprehensive training on emergency response plans, allowing all employees to participate in the training.

The Human Resources Department at Bangkok Hospital Headquarters has organized a training course titled “BLS for Non-Healthcare Provider” aimed at developing knowledge and reviewing basic life support skills for non-medical staff.
BDMS has established various programs to enhance employees’ quality of life, ensuring both physical and mental well-being.
Bangkok Hospital Headquarters launched the “BHQ Vitality & Well-Being” initiative to promote employee health and overall well-being.
BHQ Vitality & Well-Being plays a key role in enhancing employee health, productivity, and workplace satisfaction.
2,710 employees joined the program, an increase of 276 participants from the previous year.
The rise in employee engagement score to 85% suggests greater satisfaction and involvement in well-being projects.
The program significantly contributed to improved health outcomes, as evidenced by a notable reduction in BMI distribution percentages.
BNH Hospital has initiated the “Stress Relief through Yoga and Variety Dance” program.
Results from the program indicate that participating employees experienced a significant reduction in stress levels, improved work efficiency, and a better work atmosphere.

BDMS is committed to respecting of human rights and advancing a culture of Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion (DEI) within the organization by promoting professional equality and freedom of expression among employees of diverse gender identities.
BDMS encourages employees to share varied and creative ideas on medical and healthcare innovations to create new values for the country and achieve sustainable success on a global scale.
Comprehensive human rights due diligence conducted in all business unit.

BDMS received the Outstanding Role Model Organization Human Rights Award 2024 (the highest level) in the large-scale business category by the Rights and Liberties Protection Department, Ministry of Justice.
Zero cases of complaints related to discrimination, harassment, or human rights violations.
100% of employees passed human rights training.
100% of tier 1 suppliers passed human rights training.

BDMS manages and assigns the Board of Directors to devise the guidelines and enforce the Human Rights Policy to express the commitment to respecting human rights in conformity with the international standards and local regulations, such as the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGP), the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, the International Bill of Human Rights, and the Labor Protection Act B.E. 1998.
BDMS prioritizes the rights of vulnerable groups, strictly prohibits discrimination in all cases and fosters equality in all aspects of business operations.
BDMS enforces the No Child Labor, Forced Labor, and Human Trafficking Policy while respecting the rights of migrant workers and their families.
BDMS is dedicated to conducting Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) while setting out reporting channels to address complaints and ensure effective remedies in case of human rights violations.
In 2024, BDMS strived to foster Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion (DEI) based on the difference of the employees at all organizational levels.

BDMS and subsidiaries recognize this issue and are committed to continuously implementing sustainability strategies, especially in the use of renewable energy, such as solar power, to reduce reliance on non-renewable energy sources.
BDMS focuses on improving energy efficiency within the organization to ensure that energy use at every step is aligned with sustainability.
These efforts also prepare the organization to drive towards achieving the goal of Net Zero emission by 2050.
BDMS is therefore committed to being a leader in developing and implementing projects that are crucial for sustainable environmental preservation.
This infographic presents progress toward net zero emissions by 2050 and carbon neutrality (Scope 1 and Scope 2) by 2030, showing annual performance results and target tracking.
The organization is tracking its progress toward carbon neutrality and net zero emissions.
The performance results for 2023 and 2024 are explicitly stated and visually compared to the 100% target.
The status 'on track' suggests that current progress aligns with planned milestones toward the 2030 and 2050 goals.
This figure presents the breakdown of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by scope (Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3) for a total of 6.46 hundred thousand tons CO₂ equivalent (CO₂eq).
Scope 3 emissions constitute the largest share (70%) of total GHG emissions, followed by Scope 2 (25%) and Scope 1 (5%).
The company’s GHG efficiency (emissions per unit revenue) improved after 2022, stabilizing at a lower value.

One of the standards BDMS uses for this initiative is the LEED (Leadership in Energy & Environmental Design) standard, a globally recognized framework for energy-efficient and environmentally-friendly design and operations.

This initiative also prepares staff and organizations for future environmental certification to ensure environmental operations meet international standards and support the long-term sustainable development of the organization.
In 2024, 16 hospitals and subsidiaries participated in the BDMS Green Healthcare initiative.

Hospitals and companies that pass the evaluation will be fully certified according to the set goals by the end of the year, with re-accredit conducted every 3 years to ensure that all units’ environmental practices comply with the standards and align with the organization’s sustainable development approach.

claims.claim_text: Mr. Nutnapong Udomkitthaweewat, an environmental and sustainability Specialist from the Sustainability Management Department at Bangkok Dusit Medical Services Public Company Limited, was assigned as a key speaker to discuss “Climate Change and Environmental Management Awareness” for 300 employees and suppliers.
claims.section: Climate Change Awareness and Environmental Management Training

claims.claim_text: The purpose of this training is to promote learning and understanding of environmental management and climate change. It aims to enable all parts of the organization to adapt and actively participate in environmental conservation, as well as to achieve the organization’s goals for sustainable development.
claims.section: Climate Change Awareness and Environmental Management Training

claims.claim_text: Bangkok Hospital Chiang Mai installed a fresh air system within the hospital to maintain CO₂ at a required level.
With IoT technology advancement, the hospital implemented air quality sensors to measure temperature, humidity, CO₂, and PM2.5 levels and store data in the cloud with a web board display.
The upgrade helps reduce energy consumption and minimize complaints about indoor air quality.

Moreover, the initiative reduced the workload from the hourly air quality recording in temperature and humidity control rooms, such as medication and medical supply storage, while reducing expenses by 124,350 THB per year.
Quantified savings are explicitly shown: 3,467.69 USD/year, 27.57 hours/year, and 0.66 tons of CO₂/year.
The team installed the Variable Speed Drive (VSD) in the chilled water pump system to enhance its efficiency and reduce electricity costs in the hospital.
claims.section: VSD Installation for Chilled Water Pump System

claims.claim_text: Samitivej Sriracha Hospital reduced energy consumption by 248,098 kWh per year and decreased CO₂ emissions by 106 tons CO₂ eq per year.
claims.section: VSD Installation for Chilled Water Pump System

claims.claim_text: Samitivej Thonburi Hospital achieved 412,951 kWh and reduced the CO₂ emissions by 124 tons CO₂ eq per year.
claims.section: VSD Installation for Chilled Water Pump System

claims.claim_text: Bangkok Hospital Hat Yai, energy consumption was reduced by 59,213 kWh per year and carbon dioxide emissions decreased by 19 tons CO₂ eq per year.

BDMS has set sustainability goals with The target of achieving at least 50% of non-hazardous waste is utilized by 2050, supporting the circular economy and creating a long-lasting positive environmental impact.

This image is a photograph illustrating recyclable materials, with a focus on supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) 12.3, 12.4, and 12.5, which relate to responsible consumption and production.
New water bottle, no label, smaller cap, 100% recyclable.
Every 1,000,000 bottles can reduce plastic waste by 1,200 kilograms.
This plastic pellet pillow uses crushed plastic pellets from recycled plastic bottles as its main material.
The armrest pillow for blood draws has been designed to weigh 400 grams, equivalent to using four plastic bottles.
This improvement has helped reduce hospital costs by up to 12,418 THB per year.
Bangkok Hospital Udon has managed waste from the operating rooms, specifically from sterile paper packaging and sterile set wraps used to store medical instruments and supplies.
This initiative enables the hospital to recycle up to 898 kilograms of waste annually.
It has helped reduce hospital expenses by 12,000 THB per year.
BDMS is committed to maintaining a balance between water usage in business operations and the conservation of water resources.
BDMS aims to improve water management efficiency, both by reducing water consumption and enhancing water quality for specific uses.
BDMS places great importance on wastewater management, ensuring that wastewater is treated to meet national standards before being released into natural water sources.

The image visually communicates a message of environmental responsibility, specifically water conservation, and aligns with the UN SDGs 6.3 (water quality), 6.4 (water-use efficiency), and 12.2 (sustainable management of natural resources).
The infographic presents the progress toward a 2030 target to reduce water withdrawal per unit of revenue by 10% compared to the base year 2022.
Water withdrawal per unit of revenue has decreased from 5.88% in 2023 to 3.05% in 2024.
BDMS’s water withdrawal per unit revenue has decreased by 3.05% since 2022, indicating improved water use efficiency.
78.17% of water is in water-stressed areas.
Phyathai 3 Hospital has successfully reused 12,480 cubic meters of wastewater per year, resulting in a reduction of tap water costs by 224,640 baht annually.
The implementation of IoT in the wastewater treatment project primarily aims to reduce the energy consumption of aeration pumps to make them more suitable and efficient.
The results from this project include energy savings achieved by reducing the electricity consumption of aeration pumps by 20,000 kWh per year, equating to a saving of 94,000 baht per year.

Bangkok Dusit Medical Services PLC (BDMS) has published the annual Sustainability Report since 2013 to showcase the sustainability performance in healthcare and related business sectors in Thailand and abroad.

BDMS takes pride in maintaining excellence as a healthcare service and provider accredited under international standards and ensuring the highest levels of customer satisfaction in response to the expectations of all stakeholders.
The economic, social, and environmental data presented in this report covers the performance of all subsidiaries under BDMS management, as detailed in page 228 - 230.
The scope of the Sustainability Report 2024 was expanded to include data from Bangkok Hospital Pluakdaeng.
The report presents performance during the calendar year from 1st January to 31st December 2024 and complies with the Core Option outlined in the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards.

Financial data in this report are from similar sources as in Annual Report and verified by certified public accountants, whereas the Environmental, Social, and Governance performance data are verified by third party, as detailed in page 231.

The Company has set the policy that the minimum quorum of the Board of Directors should not be less than two-thirds of the total number of the Company’s directors and these directors and Sub-Committee members shall attend meetings of each group not less than 75 percent of all meetings throughout the year.
The Company has specified that each director shall hold a directorship position in the listed companies of the Stock Exchange of Thailand not exceeding 5 companies.

The Board of Directors shall ensure that the Company has set up an effective policy and guidelines in nominating and developing the senior executives of the organization and the management at all levels to possess knowledge and capability which will ultimately lead the organization towards its established goals and that they are able to perform duties in replacement of others.
The BDMS Corporate Human Resources Department will review and update the succession planning timeline on an annual basis, and submit the revised timeline to the Board of Directors for approval.

The Board of Directors and the Sub-Committees have performed self-assessment, both as a whole and as an individual on an annual basis and at least once a year to improve the utmost efficiency and effectiveness of the operation.
Overall, the assessment results of the performance of the Board as a whole, individual Board members, and subcommittees as a whole were found to be at an appropriate level.
